slides.title: The starting hypothesis (reserve now, gate the order) survives the tests, but only with a funding plan and a flexible order date

claims.claim: H1 A full order now does not fit within the covenant (Holds)
evidence: $11.0M - $2.2M committed R&D - $4.8M = $4.0M, vs a $7.0M floor (-$3.0M)

claims.claim: H2 2028 overflow can be served without the new line (Holds)
evidence: 0.6M units of overflow vs the molder's 2.5M ceiling; 5 months' notice needed; specialty volume not yet in 2028

claims.claim: H3 Demand beyond the molder's reach is credible within the line's lead time (Partly)
evidence: At forecast, 2030 overflow is 3.5M (1.0M over the ceiling). At signed minimums it is 0.9M. Two programs slipped a quarter last year

claims.claim: H4 The slot is affordable and its downside is capped (Holds)
evidence: $8.8M - $0.6M = $8.2M, still $1.2M above the floor; the most we can lose is the forfeited $0.6M

claims.claim: H5 The $4.2M balance can be funded when the order must be placed (Not yet)
evidence: No committed facility. The prepayment / signed-volume loan is uncontracted and the CFO sees it in 2028

claims.claim: H6 The slot secures timing we could not get without it (Unverified)
evidence: The slot reserves an installation crew, not capacity. The pack gives no lead time without a slot; its timeline assumes an order by June 2027

claims.claim: Revision: same direction, tighter conditions. H5 becomes a release trigger; H6 must be settled with the supplier before the March deposit.
evidence: Starting hypothesis = Operations Director's proposal: reserve the slot, release the machine only after signed orders and a liquidity review.

slides.title: Measured on accepted units, the line is already 92% utilized in 2027 and overflows from 2028; the '17% free capacity' view divides by nameplate output

claims.claim: Measured on accepted units, the line is already 92% utilized in 2027 and overflows from 2028
evidence: Ops KPI: forecast / nameplate 10.0M: 83% / 96% / 112% / 124% (2027-30)
Accepted units / practical 9.0M: 92% / 107% / 124% / 138%
Free practical capacity (M units): 0.7 / -0.6 / -2.2 / -3.4
Forecast good units: 8.3 / 9.6 / 11.2 / 12.4 (M); Nameplate 10.0M; Practical 9.0M

claims.claim: Why the Ops KPI misleads: it divides units started by nameplate hours and reports quality rejects separately, so it overstates headroom
evidence: Real 2027 slack is 0.7M units (7.8%), not 1.7M (17%)

claims.claim: Specialty runs scrap 4 points more than the standard mix, and the forecast has no allowance for it: about 0.09-0.10M units of capacity lost a year from 2029
The plant has no real buffer for 2028 peaks: whatever the decision, the bridge has to be in place before the 2028 peak.
evidence: Practical accepted capacity of 9.0M units is net of maintenance, validated changeovers and quality holds; nameplate is 10.0M.

slides.title: The size of the gap depends on unsigned demand: at forecast, overflow reaches 3.5M units by 2030; at signed minimums it is only 0.9M

claims.claim: At forecast, overflow reaches 3.5M units by 2030; at signed minimums it is only 0.9M
evidence: Chart values: Forecast 0.6 / 2.3 / 3.5; Forecast slips one year 0.7 / 2.3; Signed minimums only 0.5 / 0.9; Molder ceiling 2.5M

claims.claim: Unsigned volume: of the 12.4M units forecast for 2030, 2.6M (21%) sit above signed minimums and are nonbinding
Timing: a one-year slip pushes the molder ceiling breach from 2030 to 2031
evidence: two key design programs slipped a quarter last year

claims.claim: Mix: specialty volume adds roughly 0.1M units of overflow a year through extra scrap
Only the forecast case needs a second line before 2031. Committing $4.8M before customers sign is a bet on the top bar.
The new line is needed only if unsigned demand arrives on time, so signed volume should trigger the order.

slides.title: Annual totals understate the risk: the 98% standard is measured monthly, and with the molder maxed out, 2029 runs at 98% of monthly supply

claims.claim: The standard requires a 98% fill rate every month, for every medical-device customer; missing it twice gives the customer the right to rebid its whole supplier allocation
Annual capacity is not enough
evidence: Internal practical rate is ~0.75M units a month; the molder adds at most ~0.21M a month
Several customer launches inside one six-week window can exceed the monthly rate even when the year fits (plant supervisor)
The molder has not committed holiday-period capacity

claims.claim: With the molder maxed out, 2029 runs at 98% of monthly supply
evidence: Demand: annual forecast / 12: 0.80 / 0.93 / 1.03 (2028-30)
Demand as % of max monthly supply: 83% / 98% / 109%
How far a peak month can exceed the average: ~20% / ~2% / None: short every month

claims.claim: What is at stake: base business contribution exposed to a rebid
evidence: Base business of 9.0M units x $0.45 = ~$4.0M of annual contribution exposed to a rebid (proxy)
Losing a quarter of it costs ~$1.0M a year, more than the $0.45M lost on the 2030 forecast shortfall itself

claims.claim: A monthly simulation or an inventory buffer is needed to confirm compliance
In 2029 even the molder bridge leaves only ~2% monthly headroom: a launch cluster could trigger the two misses that open a rebid.

slides.title: Ordering the full line now would leave $4.0M of cash, $3.0M below the covenant floor, and the growth evidence offered for it does not show cause and effect

claims.claim: Ordering the full line now would leave $4.0M of cash, $3.0M below the covenant floor
evidence: Order now: 11.0 - 2.2 - 4.8 = 4.0; headroom -3.0
Reserve slot: 11.0 - 2.2 - 0.6 = 8.2; headroom +1.2
Chart: Do nothing $8.8M, Molder only $8.8M, Reserve slot $8.2M, Order line now $4.0M; Floor $7.0M

claims.claim: The Sales VP's '23% faster growth' claim does not show cause and effect
evidence: It compares companies at one point in time: the early builders also held more advance purchase commitments and sold into faster-growing therapeutic segments
It cannot show that building capacity caused the growth, and the board will not accept 'demand is growing' as a reason to breach the floor

claims.claim: With no facility, ordering in 2027 needs at least $3.0M of new funding. 'Order now' is ruled out on cash.

slides.title: Only 'reserve the slot + molder bridge' passes every hard constraint while keeping 2030 capacity available

claims.claim: Order line now fails the covenant
evidence: Fails: $4.0M; Line from ~Jan 2028; 2030 Covered; In-house; $6.45M = 4.8 + 3 x 0.55; $4.8M sunk

claims.claim: Reserve slot + molder bridge (recommended) passes every hard constraint
evidence: Passes: $8.2M; Molder, $0.07M; Covered if triggers met by Q3 2028; In-house priority; $5.8M if ordered Q1 2028; $0.6M + premium if not; Max loss $0.6M
$5.8M = $4.8M line (deposit credited) + $0.07M molder premium in 2028 + $0.14M for H1 2029 + $0.83M fixed cost for mid-2029 to 2030
$0.6M less than ordering now, because fixed costs start about 18 months later

claims.claim: Molder only is cheapest to 2029 but cannot meet forecast 2030 demand
evidence: Passes: $8.8M; Molder, $0.07M; 1.0M units short; Molder not validated; $0.65M premium + $0.45M lost (2030) + rebid risk; Fully flexible

claims.claim: Do nothing fails in the first peak
evidence: Passes: $8.8M; 0.6M unserved; 3.5M unserved; $2.9M lost contribution + rebid risk

claims.claim: Choosing 'reserve + bridge' over 'order now' costs nothing in capacity; it removes the covenant breach and a $4.8M bet on unsigned demand.

slides.title: The contract molder is a cheap bridge through 2029, but at forecast it runs out in 2030 and it cannot make the specialty product

claims.claim: The contract molder is a cheap bridge through 2029, but at forecast it runs out in 2030
evidence: Units sent to molder (M): 0.6 / 2.29 / 2.5 (cap)
Unserved units (M): 0 / 0 / 1.0
Lost contribution @ $0.45 ($M): 0 / 0 / 0.45
2028 24% of ceiling; 2029 92% of ceiling; 2030 140%: 1.0M short
2029 at 92% of the ceiling leaves 0.2M units of annual slack

claims.claim: Specialty is not validated at the molder, so it must run in-house and takes the internal slack
evidence: 20% of 2029 units, 2.24M

claims.claim: Five months' notice; holiday-period capacity not yet committed
Still worth using: serving through the molder keeps $0.33 of the $0.45 unit contribution, against $0 for a refused order
Use the molder to bridge 2028-29. It is not a substitute for the line if forecast 2030 demand arrives.

slides.title: The new line is insurance for customer allocations, not a margin play: it beats the molder on running cost only above 4.6M overflow units a year

claims.claim: It beats the molder on running cost only above 4.6M overflow units a year
evidence: 4.6M units a year = $0.55M line fixed cost / $0.12 molder premium per unit
Forecast overflow peaks at 3.5M (2030)

claims.claim: The line earns only ~$0.20M a year more than the molder in 2030
evidence: New line: 3.5M served; 3.5 x 0.45 = 1.58; fixed cost -0.55; net 1.03; 0 unserved
Molder only: 2.5M via molder; 2.5 x 0.33 = 0.83; net 0.83; 1.0M unserved (rebid trigger)
The line saves $0.12 per unit inside the ceiling, but $0.45 per unit beyond it

claims.claim: The $4.8M is justified by what it protects
evidence: Fill-rate compliance in peak months, which protects ~$4.0M a year of base contribution from rebids
In-house capacity for the specialty product the molder cannot make
Growth after 2030: each 1M units above the molder ceiling adds $0.45M a year to the line's advantage

claims.claim: Because the case rests on protecting allocations, the order trigger should be signed customer volume, not forecast margin.

slides.title: The slot is a capped option: it risks at most $0.6M, keeps $1.2M above the cash floor and pays off only if it heads off an allocation rebid

claims.claim: The slot risks at most $0.6M
evidence: Line ordered (triggers met): Credited toward the $4.8M; $0
Line not ordered: Forfeited; $0.6M
Scale check (signed-minimum case): Equals ~5.5 years of the 2030 molder premium ($0.11M)

claims.claim: Keeps $1.2M above the cash floor
evidence: $8.8M - $0.6M = $8.2M, still $1.2M above the floor. The deposit uses a third of the $1.8M headroom, leaving room for 2028-29 molder premiums ($0.35M)
The deposit does not fund the line: the $4.2M balance still needs at least $3.0M of new money

claims.claim: Pays off only if it heads off an allocation rebid
evidence: Shortfall only: 1.0M units x $0.45 = 0.45; 133%: not justified
+ rebid loses 25% of base allocation: 1.46; 41%
+ rebid loses 50% of base allocation: 2.48; 24%
It is worth paying if there is roughly a 1-in-4 to 2-in-5 chance that the slot is what keeps a customer's allocation. Today's 2.6M of unsigned 2030 volume and the 2028 overflow make that plausible

claims.claim: That chance is only real if the slot buys timing we could not otherwise get (H6)
Recommendation: pay the deposit as insurance, on condition that its order date can be deferred. Without that, the insurance lapses before funding arrives.

slides.title: Reserving the slot becomes a bad option under five conditions; the two most likely can be tested before the March deposit

claims.claim: 1 The order must be placed by June 2027, while funding is only plausible in 2028
evidence: We would have to forfeit $0.6M or breach the covenant; Negotiate an order date of Q1 2028 or later (install H1 2029); otherwise decline; Before Mar 2027

claims.claim: 2 The slot buys nothing scarce: a 12-month lead time is available without it
evidence: Paying $0.6M for timing we would get anyway; Get written lead time and crew availability without a slot; Before Mar 2027

claims.claim: 3 Demand stays near signed minimums
evidence: Overflow of 0.9M or less through 2030; molder covers it for $0.11M a year or less; Track signed volume quarterly; kill at the go/no-go gate; Gate 2

claims.claim: 4 Programs slip a year
evidence: The line arrives a year early and carries $0.55M a year of fixed cost before it is needed; Use the deferral right; molder covers 2030 at 92% of its ceiling; Gate 2

claims.claim: 5 Cash headroom erodes in 2027
evidence: The deposit uses $0.6M of $1.8M headroom; pre-build stock and validation compete for the rest; 13-week cash forecast; cap pre-build working capital; Monthly

claims.claim: If the supplier will not move the order date to Q1 2028 or later, decline the slot and plan on the molder plus a 2028 order at standard lead time, once that lead time is confirmed.
evidence: The pack gives no slot expiry or deferral terms; the June 2027 order date comes from the stated 'if ordered by June 2027, machine expected mid-2028'.

slides.title: Cover 2028 in three layers: the contract molder booked by June 2027, a 2027 safety stock, and specialty kept in-house

claims.claim: A. External capacity: contract molder
evidence: Book 0.6M units for 2028 (24% of the ceiling), about $0.07M of premium
Formal notice is 5 months, but sign by 30 June 2027 to lock in holiday-period capacity
Hold an option on up to 2.3M units for 2029 (~$0.27M)
Get a quote and timeline for specialty first-article validation as a hedge

claims.claim: B. Internal buffer: 2027 safety stock
evidence: 2027 has 0.7M units of practical slack (9.0M - 8.3M), more than the 2028 overflow
Pre-build standard containers ahead of the 2028 peak to absorb launch clustering
Depends on shelf-life and customer lot rules; cap the working capital so cash headroom holds

claims.claim: C. Internal mix: protect what only we can make
evidence: Schedule specialty first on the own line; the molder is not validated for it
Add a 4-point specialty scrap allowance to the plan (~0.1M units a year)
Run a monthly fill-rate simulation (launch windows, holidays, scrap) by Q2 2027

claims.claim: 2028 coverage check
evidence: Contract molder: 2.5 available; 0.6 (24%); $0.07M premium
2027 safety stock from practical slack: up to 0.7; Peak-month buffer; Working capital (unit cost not in pack)
Total cover vs 0.6M forecast overflow: 3.2; ~5x the overflow; Fixed capex: $0

claims.claim: Only a January 2027 order, which breaches the covenant, gets the line in before the 2028 peak; any compliant order arrives after it, so 2028 needs this bridge.

slides.title: Release the $4.2M balance only when all three triggers are met: demand, funding and readiness

claims.claim: Demand: Signed 2029 or 2030 minimums of 10.5M units or more (today 9.4M / 9.8M), including take-or-pay or prepaid volume; OR: the monthly simulation shows 2+ months below 98% with the molder at its contracted capacity
evidence: Why 10.5M: signed overflow (~1.6M) would already use two-thirds of the molder ceiling, and fewer than half of the remaining 1.9M unsigned forecast units would exhaust it
Internal capacity after specialty scrap ~8.9M + molder 2.5M = ~11.4M of demand coverable without the line.

claims.claim: Funding: At least $3.5M of committed funding, so cash after the $4.2M payment is $7.5M or more
evidence: $8.2M - $4.2M = $4.0M; plus $3.5M = $7.5M, i.e. the $7.0M floor plus a $0.5M buffer
Sources: customer prepayment, or a supplemental loan backed by a signed-volume guarantee; pricing to be negotiated

claims.claim: Readiness: Supplier confirms installation within 12 months of order at a fixed price; specialty validation plan in place
evidence: Plan allows +2 months for specialty validation
Molder bridge contracted through commissioning
Construction inflation re-quoted

claims.claim: Not triggers: 'demand is growing', nonbinding forecasts, peer growth statistics, or a wish to announce capacity publicly.
One customer contract can meet two triggers at once: a signed-volume guarantee raises committed demand and secures the loan.

slides.title: Four decision gates separate the provisional reservation from the full investment

claims.claim: Gate 0 (Jan 2027 IC, CEO / IC): Approve the $0.6M deposit, conditional on supplier terms; start the molder RFQ and funding workstream; no full order, no public announcement
evidence: If ordered here: line producing ~mid-2028, after the 2028 peak starts

claims.claim: Gate 0b (Feb-Mar 2027, Procurement / Ops): Supplier confirms an order date of Q1 2028 or later and the lead time in writing; pay the deposit in March, or decline if terms fail
Gate 1 (By Jun 2027, Operations): Molder signed for 2028, including the holiday period; monthly simulation complete; early order only if all 3 triggers are met
Gate 2 (Q1 2028 target, IC (CFO case)): Go/no-go on the $4.2M balance; Go: line producing by about mid-2029 and relieves the 2029 peak; No-go: book 2029 molder volume
evidence: If ordered here: producing ~Q1-Q2 2029 (+2 months validation)

claims.claim: Gate 3 (Q3 2028 last date, IC): Last order date for a line producing before 2030; No-go: forfeit $0.6M, extend the molder, re-gate for 2031
evidence: If ordered here: producing ~Q3-Q4 2029, just before 2030
Line timing = 12-month lead time + commissioning; the specialty product may need 2 more months of validation

claims.claim: Provisional (Gates 0-1): $0.6M at risk, cash at or above $8.2M | Full investment (Gates 2-3): $4.2M, only with at least $3.5M committed funding
Each gate has a date, a proposed owner and a default: if a trigger is missed, the default is the cheaper, reversible path.

slides.title: If customer orders fall short, the plan degrades gracefully: in the weak-demand cases the worst outcome is a $0.6M forfeited deposit, never a covenant breach

claims.claim: The cash floor holds in every case. Weak demand costs at most $0.6M
evidence: Forecast, funded (0.6 / 2.3 / 3.5): No: 1.0M short in 2030; Triggers met: order Q1 2028; ~$5.8M incl. line; $7.5M (+0.5)
One-year slip (0 / 0.7 / 2.3): Yes: 92% of ceiling in 2030; Defer the slot; re-gate for 2031; $0.36M premium (+$0.6M if no deferral); ~$7.8M (+0.8)
Signed minimums only (0 / 0.5 / 0.9): Yes: 36% of ceiling or less; Kill at Gate 2; forfeit deposit; $0.6M + $0.16M premium; ~$8.0M (+1.0)

Forecast demand, no funding (0.6 / 2.3 / 3.5): No: 1.0M short in 2030; No order (the floor holds); molder to cap, safety stock, ration; $0.6M + $0.65M premium + $0.45M lost + rebid risk; ~$7.6M (+0.6)
Calculation, signed case: $8.8M - $0.6M deposit - $0.16M premiums = ~$8.0M. Slip: $8.8M - $0.6M - $0.36M = ~$7.8M. No-funding: $8.8M - $0.6M - $0.65M = ~$7.6M.

claims.claim: The case to watch is the last one: demand arrives but funding does not. The board's rule (no breach of the floor) then means accepting 2030 rebid risk.
The mitigation is to make customer co-funding (prepayment or a volume guarantee) the price of guaranteed capacity, starting in 2027 negotiations.
The unfunded forecast case is a customer-retention risk, not a cash risk.

slides.title: The answer is most sensitive to unsigned demand timing, funding and the slot's terms; each is covered by a gate or a test before the deposit

claims.claim: Demand above signed minimums (2.6M units in 2030) and program slips decides whether the line is needed before 2031
evidence: Demand trigger on signed volume; quarterly tracking; Gate 3 last date

claims.claim: Funding: prepayment / guarantee not contracted; debt pricing not negotiated. Without it, no order can be placed
evidence: Funding trigger of $3.5M or more; CFO term sheet by Gate 2

claims.claim: Slot terms: order date, deferral, lead time without a slot (not in pack) decide whether the deposit buys anything
evidence: Condition precedent before the March payment

claims.claim: Monthly peaks, launch clustering, molder holiday capacity uncommitted: fill-rate misses even when annual capacity fits
evidence: Monthly simulation; 2027 safety stock; holiday capacity in the molder contract

claims.claim: Specialty: +2 months' validation; 4-point scrap allowance missing from forecast: line later and capacity ~0.1M units lower
evidence: Allowance built in; 14-month line timeline; molder validation quote

claims.claim: Construction inflation; no salvage value; 2027-30 operating cash flow (not in pack): capex and cash tests could move
evidence: Fixed-price re-quote at Gate 2; 13-week cash forecast

claims.claim: No single uncertainty overturns the recommendation; together they explain why the $4.2M must wait for evidence.

slides.title: We ask the committee for four decisions in January, none of which commits the $4.2M balance

claims.claim: 1 Approve the $0.6M slot deposit for March 2027, on one condition
evidence: Written supplier terms allowing an order date of Q1 2028 or later and confirming the lead time. If refused, decline the slot.

claims.claim: 2 Decline the full line order and any public capacity announcement now
evidence: Instead, let Sales use the reserved slot and molder plan privately to turn nonbinding forecasts into signed minimums or prepayments.

claims.claim: 3 Authorize the 2028 overflow plan
evidence: Contract molder for 0.6M units, signed by June 2027 with holiday capacity; capped 2027 safety stock; specialty validation quote.

claims.claim: 4 Adopt the three release triggers and the gate calendar
evidence: Demand of 10.5M units or more signed, or a simulated breach; at least $3.5M committed funding; readiness confirmed. Target Q1 2028, last date Q3 2028.

claims.claim: Total cash committed by these decisions: $0.6M, leaving $8.2M against the $7.0M floor.

slides.title: Appendix A: every figure in the deck traces to briefing-pack inputs through these calculations

claims.claim: Every figure in the deck traces to briefing-pack inputs through these calculations
evidence: Cash available above commitments: $11.0M - $2.2M approved validation/R&D = $8.8M (headroom $1.8M)
Order line now: $8.8M - $4.8M = $4.0M; -$3.0M vs floor
Reserve slot, then order: $8.8M - $0.6M = $8.2M; - $4.2M balance = $4.0M (deposit not double-counted); Needs $3.0M or more new funding
Practical utilization: 8.3 / 9.6 / 11.2 / 12.4 divided by 9.0M = 92% / 107% / 124% / 138%
Specialty scrap allowance: 20% x 11.2M x 4% (2029); 20% x 12.4M x 4% (2030); assumed 0 in 2028 = 0.09M / 0.10M units
Forecast overflow: Demand - 9.0M + scrap allowance = 0.6 / 2.29 / 3.50M (2028-30)
Line vs molder break-even: $0.55M / $0.12 = 4.6M units a year
2030 line vs molder: 3.5 x 0.45 - 0.55 = 1.03 vs 2.5 x (0.45 - 0.12) = 0.83; Line +$0.20M a year before capex
Recommended path, 2027-30 cost: 4.8 + 0.07 + 0.14 (H1 2029 premium) + 0.55 x 1.5 years = ~$5.8M (vs $6.45M order-now)
Slot break-even probability: $0.6M / (0.45 + share x 9.0M x 0.45) = 133% / 41% / 24%
Reproducible in deliverable/supporting/calc.py.

slides.title: Appendix B: judgment calls made where the pack was silent; each is flagged so the committee can challenge it

claims.claim: Judgment calls made where the pack was silent
evidence: 2027-30 operating cash flow: Excluded; cash tests use commitments against $8.8M; Positive cash flow would ease the funding trigger
Slot expiry and deferral terms: Assume an order by June 2027 unless renegotiated; made a condition of the deposit; If deferral is already allowed, the case for the slot gets stronger
Specialty share in 2028 and 2030: 0% in 2028; 20% in 2030 (same as 2029); +/-0.1M units of overflow
Timing of the 2028 peak: About Q2 2028 (pack: before mid-2028); Earlier peak brings the molder notice date forward
Contribution at risk from a rebid: $0.45/unit on the 9.0M base; 25% / 50% illustrative losses; Changes break-even, not direction
Demand trigger and cash buffer: 10.5M signed units; $0.5M above the floor; Policy choices; the committee may tighten or relax them
Downside cases: Slip = forecast delayed one year; weak case = signed minimums; Other paths fall between these

claims.claim: These choices were made without access to management; the committee should confirm or replace them.

normalized.recommendation: Reserve the slot as a capped $0.6M option, bridge 2028 with the contract molder, and order the line only once signed demand and funding clear set triggers. Decisions requested: (1) Approve the $0.6M slot deposit for March 2027, on condition of written supplier terms allowing an order date of Q1 2028 or later and confirming the lead time; if refused, decline the slot. (2) Decline the full line order and any public capacity announcement now. (3) Authorize the 2028 overflow plan: contract molder for 0.6M units, signed by June 2027 with holiday capacity; capped 2027 safety stock; specialty validation quote.
